newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq hopes Syria opens pipeline for oil exports.
newsitem.headline: Iraq hopes Syria opens pipeline for oil exports.

text.p: Iraq hopes Syria will reopen a pipeline via its territory for Iraqi oil exports, Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said on Friday.

"We hope in the light of latest atmosphere concerning the opening of commercial co-operation between Syria and Iraq that the Syrian leadership will reconsider a decision it took in the past to enable us export oil via Syria," the minister said in a news conference in Baghdad.

Rasheed said the pipeline system linking Iraq's Kirkuk oilfields to the Mediterranean terminals of Banias in Syria and Tripoli in Lebanon only needed minor repairs that Iraqi technicians were capable of doing.
The Syrian government closed the pipeline in 1982 and has been shut since then.
A Syrian trade delegation was in Baghdad early this month in the first such visit since the early 1980s. Iraqi officials gave the delegation a red carpet welcome.
The countries ruled by rival wings of Arab Baath party have shown signs of rapprochement recently and Syrian products can now be found in shops in Baghdad and other Iraqi provinces.
The 700,000 barrel per day (bpd) pipeline was used to export between 450,000 bpd and 600,000 of Iraqi crude before the Syrians closed it down.
Rasheed said the pipeline, if repaired properly, could carry up to one million barrels per day.
